title: Finite cover with analytically unramified maximal localizations
statement: Let $R$ be a normal Nagata domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring] [def-weil-pbc-nagata-ring], $K$ its fraction field, $x\in K$, $S=R[x]\subseteq K$, $\mathfrak m$ a maximal ideal of $S$, and $A=S_{\mathfrak m}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Assume the following local calculation for every normal Nagata domain $R\prime$ and its fraction field $K\prime$: if $R\prime$ and $R\prime[y]$ are Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and a maximal ideal $\mathfrak q$ of $R\prime[y]$ contains $y$, then $R\prime[y]_{\mathfrak q}$ is analytically unramified [def-weil-pbc-analytically-unramified]. Then there exists a Noetherian domain $B$ with an injective $A$-algebra map, finite as an $A$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], such that (i) for some nonzero $f\in B$, every prime localization of $B_f$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away] is a normal domain, and (ii) every maximal localization of $B$ is analytically unramified. In Lean, the quantified local-calculation rings and the witness B lie in Type(max u v); the finite splitting construction fits in this universe.

proof.text: Fix $\mathfrak m$ and set $\mathfrak n=R\cap\mathfrak m$. The field $\kappa(\mathfrak m)$ is generated as a $\kappa(\mathfrak n)$-algebra by the residue of $x$, because $S=R[x]$; it is finite over $\kappa(\mathfrak n)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-zariski-lemma]. Let $\bar f(T)=T^d+\sum_{i=1}^d\bar c_iT^{d-i}\in\kappa(\mathfrak n)[T]$ be the monic minimal polynomial of the residue of $x$. Lift each $\bar c_i$ to a fraction $c_i/s_i\in R_{\mathfrak n}$ with $s_i\in R\setminus\mathfrak n$; localize $R$ and $S$ at the product $s=\prod_i s_i$, so all lifts lie in $R_s$. The resulting monic $f(T)\in R_s[T]$ has $f(x)\in\mathfrak mS_s$, since its residue in $\kappa(\mathfrak m)$ is $\bar f(\bar x)=0$. The maximal ideal $\mathfrak mS_s$ and its localization of $S$ still give the original $S_{\mathfrak m}$.

proof.text: Work over the localized $R_s$ and rename it $R$. Adjoin roots of $f$ successively to $K$; at most $d$ finite algebraic extensions give a finite splitting field $K''/K$. Let $R'$ be the integral closure of $R$ in $K''$. The Nagata property of $R$ [lem-weil-pbc-nagata-localization] makes $R'$ a finite $R$-module by the N-2 clause of [def-weil-pbc-nagata-ring] and [def-weil-pbc-japanese-domain]; it is a normal domain with fraction field $K''$ by [lem-weil-pbc-integral-closure-finite-extension-normal], and Nagata by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-nagata-nagata]. Every root of the monic polynomial $f$ is integral over $R$, so lies in $R'$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. Put $S'=R'[x]\subset K''$. The same finitely many $R$-module generators of $R'$ generate $S'$ as an $S$-module, so $S\subseteq S'$ is finite [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], hence integral by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral]. Every maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ of $S$ has a prime ideal of $S'$ above it by [lem-weil-pbc-integral-injective-lying-over], and that prime is maximal by [lem-weil-pbc-integral-prime-over-maximal-maximal].

Set A=S_m and B=(S\setminus m)^{-1}S' after the denominator localization and splitting extension. The denominator localization is already inverted in A, so B is finite over A, injective, and a Noetherian domain. Every maximal ideal of B comes from a maximal ideal m' of S' over m, because a finite extension is integral and maximal ideals contract to maximal ideals.

For each such m', the split polynomial evaluates into m', so one factor x-r lies in m'. Since R'[x]=R'[x-r], apply the hypothesis giving analytic unramifiedness of generator-containing maximal localizations. Iterated localization identifies these with the maximal localizations of B.

Writing the original x=b/a with a nonzero, inverting its image identifies S'_a with R'_a. Thus B_a is a localization of the normal domain R', and all its prime localizations are normal domains. Injectivity makes the image of a nonzero.
